title: The Burnt Safehouse
premise: Ines Crane, a whistle-blower living under four names, works deniable cases for a broker who never gives a real name. When the safe house she's hidden in for two years is listed online with interior photos — her own handwriting visible on the whiteboard — Ines realizes someone inside her protection chain is selling her out. Following the listing's digital trail, she uncovers a plot to destroy a summit hotel with a gas 'accident' timed to kill a witness who can expose the broker's network. To stop it, Ines must burn every alias, ally with the federal agent hunting her, and finally choose one name to live under. The attack is prevented at devastating cost: the broker escapes, but Ines testifies openly, trading survival in the shadows for a fragile, public belonging.
about_author: Juniper Ishikawa is a former risk analyst who spent a decade writing security assessments before turning to fiction. She writes thrillers about people whose identities are their most dangerous possessions.

chapters.title: Four Names
chapters.summary: Ines Crane's POV. A routine morning in the safe house establishes her rituals of anonymity: rotating names, no photos, cash only. She takes a small case through her broker and we feel her competence and loneliness. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath routine.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: Ines POV. Scrolling property sites out of boredom, she finds the safe house listed for sale — with interior photos showing her whiteboard, her coat, her handwriting. Panic sets in as she verifies it's real and current. Emotional beat: violation; the walls of her life dissolving.

chapters.title: Contact Protocol
chapters.summary: Ines POV. She attempts emergency contact with her broker using dead-drop protocols that return nothing. She packs a go-bag while cataloguing what the photos revealed. Emotional beat: the discipline of fear; she realizes protocol itself may be compromised.

chapters.title: Agent Vasquez
chapters.summary: Dana Vasquez's POV. A federal agent reviewing cold whistle-blower cases notices the same property listing flagged by an automated watch program. She recognizes the safe house from an old file — and the woman who vanished from it. Emotional beat: hunter's curiosity sharpening into urgency.

chapters.title: Run Light
chapters.summary: Ines POV. Ines flees to a secondary bolt-hole, shedding her third identity en route. She replays who knew the address and narrows suspects to three people inside her protection chain. Emotional beat: grief for the self she has to abandon again.

chapters.title: The Broker's Silence
chapters.summary: Ines POV. Using a burner, Ines reaches a cutout who passes a message upward; the reply is a single word: 'Stay.' She refuses, sensing the instruction is containment, not protection. Emotional beat: first open defiance of the system that saved her.

chapters.title: Photos Don't Lie
chapters.summary: Vasquez POV. Vasquez pulls metadata from the listing: uploaded via a device registered to a private security contractor tied to summit logistics. Her request to escalate is quietly denied. Emotional beat: institutional rot made personal.

chapters.title: The Witness
chapters.summary: Ines POV. Digging into the contractor, Ines finds a pattern: another protected witness, Marek Solin, scheduled to testify at the summit's anti-corruption panel. She understands why the house was exposed — to flush her toward him or away. Emotional beat: the case becomes hers by choice.

chapters.title: Two Shadows
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Vasquez traces Ines to a transit hub; Ines spots the surveillance tail and executes a textbook evasion — then deliberately leaves a message only Vasquez could read. Emotional beat: a gambit; prey choosing its predator.

chapters.title: Terms
chapters.summary: Ines and Vasquez POV, alternating within a tense café meeting. Ines offers information on the contractor in exchange for Vasquez going off-book. Neither trusts the other; both need each other. Emotional beat: wary alliance forged from mutual isolation.

chapters.title: Marek
chapters.summary: Marek Solin's POV. The witness lives in gilded protective custody, chafing, unaware his testimony matters more than his safety. He notices his handlers changed last week. Emotional beat: dread without vocabulary; he feels the trap closing.

chapters.title: The Contractor
chapters.summary: Ines POV. Ines infiltrates the contractor's records via a laundering front and finds the summit hotel's maintenance contracts were rewritten six weeks ago — gas line work scheduled during the opening night. Emotional beat: cold clarity; the accident has a date.

chapters.title: What the Photos Sold
chapters.summary: Vasquez POV. Vasquez identifies the photographer: a junior protection officer who died in a car crash nine days after the shoot. Officially alcohol. Emotionally, this confirms the conspiracy kills its own. Beat: guilt — she reviewed and closed that file.

chapters.title: Safe House Two
chapters.summary: Ines POV. Ines shelters with Vasquez in an unlisted location, breaking her own rule against partners. They compare files; the broker's silence now looks like complicity or captivity. Emotional beat: intimacy as risk; trust as a calculated bet.

chapters.title: The Fourth Name
chapters.summary: Ines POV. Flashback chapter: how Ines became Ines Crane, the night she blew the whistle and lost everything, told as she decides whether to use her original name — her real one — to access old credentials. Beat: identity as wound and weapon.

chapters.title: Gas and Glass
chapters.summary: Marek POV. Marek's new handler walks him through the hotel 'for familiarity.' Marek notices fresh pipe fittings behind an access panel and says nothing — but photographs them. Beat: a coward choosing courage in secret.

chapters.title: Deniable Assets
chapters.summary: Ines POV. Ines maps the operation's personnel: contractors, a fixer named Okafor, and a coordinator whose comms route through servers her broker once used. The overlap is undeniable. Beat: betrayal confirmed; the person who hid her sold her.

chapters.title: Okafor
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. The fixer runs errands for a man he's never met, uneasy about the summit job's civilian count. He begins keeping his own insurance file. Beat: complicity cracking under conscience.

chapters.title: Tail Lights
chapters.summary: Vasquez POV. Vasquez's off-book queries trip an internal flag; she's suspended pending review. She chooses to keep working anyway, burning her career in real time. Beat: point of no return; the price of survival made concrete.

chapters.title: The Summit Schedule
chapters.summary: Ines POV. Cross-referencing the gas work window with the summit agenda, Ines pinpoints the attack: opening gala night, when the hotel's east wing will be full and the witness on stage. Beat: ticking clock installed; eleven days.

chapters.title: Message from the Dark
chapters.summary: Ines POV. The broker finally contacts Ines directly: a voice-altered call warning her off, promising restoration of her old life if she walks away. She hears a background sound — a harbor bell — and geolocates it. Beat: temptation offered and refused.

chapters.title: Harbor Light
chapters.summary: Ines and Vasquez POV. Surveillance of the harbor building reveals the broker's operational hub — and evidence the attack is designed to also destroy the server archive holding every whistle-blower's file, including Ines's real identity. Beat: stakes double; it's not just murder, it's erasure.

chapters.title: Marek's Message
chapters.summary: Marek POV. Marek smuggles his pipe-fitting photos to a journalist's dead drop; the drop is watched, and his handler intercepts him. He talks his way out — barely — but now they know he noticed. Beat: terror; the mouse has squeaked.

chapters.title: The Mole's Face
chapters.summary: Vasquez POV. Vasquez identifies the insider who leaked the safe house listing: a supervisor in the witness-protection liaison office, photographed entering the harbor hub. Beat: righteous fury; the protector was the predator.

chapters.title: Nine Days
chapters.summary: Ines POV. Planning montage: Ines drafts three interlocking plans — evacuate the gala, expose the plot publicly, or sabotage the gas system. Each requires something she doesn't have. Beat: strategic tension; imperfect options weighed.

chapters.title: Recruiting Marek
chapters.summary: Ines and Marek POV. Ines makes contact with Marek through his one trusted habit — a morning swim. She tells him the truth; he must decide whether to help trap his own protectors. Beat: two survivors recognizing each other.

chapters.title: The Archive Key
chapters.summary: Ines POV. Ines learns the archive server needs physical authentication — a keycard held by the mole. Stealing it means confirming their suspicions and triggering the timeline early. Beat: deliberate provocation as strategy.

chapters.title: Triggered
chapters.summary: Okafor POV. The keycard theft is discovered; the operation accelerates from nine days to four. Okafor is assigned to the gas crew and realizes he's being set up as the fall guy. Beat: panic in the machine; a cog deciding to jam it.

chapters.title: Bargaining with a Ghost
chapters.summary: Ines POV. Ines confronts the broker's voice directly via hijacked channel, offering him the fall in exchange for calling off the attack. His answer reveals he isn't the top — he's afraid of someone above. Beat: the conspiracy has a ceiling she can't see.

chapters.title: Suspension Broken
chapters.summary: Vasquez POV. Vasquez burns her badge, going fully rogue, and brings one loyal colleague, Reyes, into the plan. Beat: sacrifice crystallized; she chooses the mission over the institution.

chapters.title: Three Days
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converging. Final preparations: Marek will speak at the gala as bait, Vasquez's team will cover exits, Ines will hit the archive room during the toast. Okafor sends them the gas schematics anonymously. Beat: coiled readiness; everyone all-in.

chapters.title: Gala Night
chapters.summary: Marek POV. The summit opens in crystal and champagne. Marek takes the stage, scanning faces, knowing the air around him may be counting down. Beat: dread dressed in evening wear.

chapters.title: The Toast
chapters.summary: Ines POV. As glasses rise, Ines breaches the service corridors toward the archive room, passing the gas crew moving into position. A guard rotation she didn't expect blocks the stairwell. Beat: plan meeting reality; improvisation under adrenaline.

chapters.title: Archive Fire
chapters.summary: Ines POV. Ines reaches the server room as the mole initiates early purge. She physically fights to preserve the drives, taking a knife wound, and forces the mole to flee — leaving his keycard and phone behind. Beat: cost paid in blood; partial victory.

chapters.title: Vent
chapters.summary: Vasquez and Okafor POV. Vasquez's team intercepts the gas release at the riser valve with ninety seconds to spare; Okafor, turning on his employers, takes a bullet shielding Reyes. Beat: heroism from the least likely; the attack dies in the pipes.

chapters.title: Stage Light
chapters.summary: Marek POV. With the plot failing, Marek abandons his prepared remarks and tells the summit, live, that someone tried to kill them all tonight — naming the contractor. The room erupts; cameras catch everything. Beat: witness becomes testimony; secrecy ends.

chapters.title: The Man Above
chapters.summary: Ines POV. The mole's phone leads to the true principal — a summit organizer himself — arrested trying to board a charter. The broker vanishes, files wiped, a ghost again. Beat: justice incomplete; the escape that keeps the world honest.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Ines POV. Weeks later, Ines sits before a hearing and uses her real name aloud for the first time in years, entering the recovered archive into record so every erased whistle-blower is restored. Beat: catharsis; identity reclaimed as gift, not wound.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Vasquez POV. Vasquez, reinstated under protest, visits Ines in a city where neither hides anymore. Their alliance settles into something like friendship. Marek rebuilds his life; Okafor recovers. Beat: belonging earned; the price acknowledged.

chapters.title: One Name
chapters.summary: Ines POV. Epilogue: Ines stands before the sold safe house — new owners, new paint — and lets the last alias go. She keeps only one name, her own, and walks into an ordinary street unhidden. Beat: resolution; survival transformed into living.
